sourceName: Tạp chí Công Thương (TPBank vay tín chấp 900 triệu)
notes: Article is about TPBank 'vay tín chấp' (salary-linked discount mentioned: lower rate for salary transfer of 7.5M+/month), not explicitly the product named 'theo lương'. It is 2 years old; the 0.6%/month floor (7.2%/yr) looks unusually low and may be a promotional or salary-account rate. Basis not stated. Article says no other fees ('không phát sinh phụ phí'); amount 8-18x monthly salary. Other sources disagree: viettelmoney.vn/so-sanh-lai-suat-vay/ (undated, ~Dec 2025) lists TPBank unsecured '10,8% đến 17%/năm' (lender_general, basis/term not stated); VPBank's own blog dated 2025-08-19 lists TPBank 'Từ 1.6%/ tháng', max 70M, 36 months (competitor source). Chose this one for product-level detail and higher max (18%/yr vs 17%) but it is the oldest; treat the floor with caution.

sourceName: VPBank blog 'Top 8 ngân hàng cho vay tín chấp' (competitor lender article)
notes: Source describes a generic TPBank unsecured loan, not TPFico by name; max 70M and 36 months are from the same bullet list. It is a floor ('từ') only, no maximum. Written by a competitor (VPBank) so treat with care. Basis not stated. Sapo.vn article (2025-03-06) about 'Sapo Money' online loan via TPBank says 'từ 2,75%/tháng', up to 70M, 6-36 months, but that is a merchant-platform program for Sapo sellers, not TPFico, so not used. Sapo article of 2023-09-11 says online unsecured interest is on 'dư nợ giảm dần' in general, not tied to TPBank. No TPFico-specific rate found on any page fetched.

No rate found. Searched Vietnamese for TPBank + FPT Telecom installment; results only show FPT Telecom autopay via TPBank and 0% installment programs from Home Credit/Techcombank at FPT Shop, none for this product. Do not substitute the general TPBank unsecured rate.

sourceName: VIB product landing page: Vay tiêu dùng tín chấp
notes: Official VIB page, undated, covers VIB's unsecured consumer loan in general and does not say whether it is the salary-via-VIB variant or the credit-card variant (income by bank transfer required, min 5M civil servants / 7M others). Basis not stated on the page. The existing official research found the VIB calculator applying 23-25%/year (about 1.92-2.08%/month), which is slightly above this page's 1.9%/month maximum; the 1.29%/month floor (about 15.5%/yr) was not in the earlier notes. Other secondary values: VPBank blog 2025-08-19 lists VIB 'Từ 14%/năm', max 600M, 60 months; viettelmoney.vn comparison lists VIB unsecured 17%/năm (undated). Chose the official page (highest maximum among sources that give a range). Same figures apply to the sibling VIB product.

sourceName: VIB product landing page: Vay tiêu dùng tín chấp
notes: Same page and caveats as vib-vay-tin-chap-nhan-luong-qua-vib: the page does not distinguish the salary-transfer or credit-card variants, so this range may not be specific to this product. Basis not stated. The official calculator (existing research) used 24-25%/yr (about 2.0-2.1%/month), above this page's 1.9%/month maximum; a contradiction within VIB's own pages, unresolved.

sourceName: VIB Super Cash: biểu phí, điều kiện
notes: Basis still NOT found. Fetched official fee page, official EN page, VNEconomy (2026-01-12) and Thị trường Tài chính Tiền tệ (2025-07-22): none says reducing or flat. EN page only says 'Fixed monthly repayment', which describes the instalment, not the interest basis. Contradiction: the press article (https://thitruongtaichinhtiente.vn/print/69066.html, 2025-07-22) says 'từ 425 đồng/triệu/ngày (tương đương 15,5–22,5%/năm)', and the official EN page also shows 'From only 425 VND per million VND per day' beside the 1.63%-2.5%/month, which is about 1.28%/month, below the stated range; unexplained. Kept the monthly range because it is on the official fee page and has the higher maximum. Amount 3M-1B and term 'from 1 day to 5 years' from the official EN page (https://www.vib.com.vn/en/super-cash); 1 day cannot be expressed in months so termMin is null. Early settlement and limit-change fees: free (official fee page). The 425đ/day figure being a daily rate hints that interest accrues daily on actual balance, but that is my inference, not stated, so basis stays unknown.
